protocol.selection: Previously measured compact entries plus fastest published time and all ties in the October 8 pinned tables. Rounded minute times retain every tie. LuaJIT tests every unchanged listed Lua source for local compatibility and speed.
protocol.fastest_claim: Fastest measured among this selected cohort, not an exhaustive local sweep of every scripting source. Published-fastest variants are explicitly covered or excluded with reasons.
protocol.source_metric: Nonblank, noncomment physical LOC of the complete unchanged listed program. General runtime libraries excluded.
protocol.timed_region: Sequential fresh process through exit, including interpreter/JIT startup, workers and complete stdout to a regular file. Output validation is outside timing.
protocol.python_runtime: New parallel Python invocations explicitly use the fork multiprocessing start policy assumed by the upstream Linux programs. The general launcher is included in process timing.
protocol.linux_cpu_probe: New Ruby and Perl invocations redirect only /proc/cpuinfo reads to a pinned eight-logical-CPU fixture on macOS. These general portability preloads are timed; complete benchmark sources are unchanged.
protocol.normalization: Raw process medians on the same Apple M3 with AC power and Low Power Mode off. Earlier compact medians are preserved. Each new benchmark batch includes three fresh samples of a preserved native control to audit drift; no rescaling.
protocol.compiler_guard: Before samples wait for no competing compiler >=5% CPU. Inspect compiler executable names and power at both boundaries and every 10 seconds; discard affected samples.
